title: The Permutative / Apposition (Al-Badal)
source: Original instructional lesson authored for this application (syllabus ref: Haywood & Nahmad Ch. 46; Ryding Ch. 9 §9.2)
objectives: Identify apposition (al-badal) and its antecedent (al-mubdal minhu).
Distinguish the three types of badal: identical replacement, part-of-whole, and inclusive quality.
Ensure exact case agreement between the badal and its antecedent.
recallPrompt: From Chapter 10: In هٰذَا الكِتَابُ مُفِيدٌ, what is the syntactic relationship of الكِتَابُ to هٰذَا?

sections.heading: Apposition in Classical Arabic (Al-Badal)
sections.body: Al-badal (the permutative / appositive) places a second noun directly after an antecedent (al-mubdal minhu) to clarify, rename, or specify it—common in titles ('the Caliph ʿUmar'), demonstrative phrases ('this book'), and partitive expressions ('I read the book, half of it').

sections.label: Case Agreement of Al-Badal
sections.summary: The badal ALWAYS takes the exact same grammatical case (nominative, accusative, or genitive) as its antecedent (al-mubdal minhu).

sections.heading: Three Types of Al-Badal
rows: I read the book, half of it (both accusative)
The teacher benefited me—his knowledge (both nominative)

sections.translation: I read half of the book.
sections.irab: الكِتَابَ: مَفْعُولٌ بِهِ مَنْصُوبٌ | نِصْفَ: بَدَلُ بَعْضٍ مِنْ كُلٍّ مَنْصُوبٌ (تَابِعٌ لِلْكِتَابِ) | ـهُ: مُضَافٌ إِلَيْهِ
sections.notes: In part-of-whole and inclusive badal, a pronoun (ـهُ) links the badal back to the antecedent.

sections.heading: Titles Before Names
sections.body: Whenever a title or role precedes a proper name (النَّبِيُّ مُحَمَّدٌ, الإِمَامُ مَالِكٌ), the proper name is badal matching the title's case.
